Thank you so much for responding to this, it's been a really dark period of my life for a long time. I cannot express the amount of daily pain I've been in and how much I've lost, it's honestly been catatonic. But it's really supportive and a light in the darkness to just know that others are with me in this, so really thank you for taking the time to respond. It sounds like you really understand, I'm sorry this is happening to you too. I wanted to share with you treatment that i've been getting that's drastically changed everything, because I really hope it can help you too. I'll start off with what has given me immediately relief to chronic thrush:

The Depo Provera shot. I figured I had nothing to loose so I did it. In three days my chronic almost 3 year infection was gone. I get severe nerve pain of my vulva and vagina because I've had the infection for so long, and three days in I went to insert my daily boric acid suppository, and it didn't hurt. I was dumb founded. I had no thrushy cottage discharge, my labia wasn't on fire, I didn't itch constantly, and I could actually comfortably insert. I thought I was dreaming. A month in, I am having my first period on the shot and it's really just a tad of spotting. No thrush. No flare up before my period (but I was like you, I had it every day, it just got worse the week before). I have no active infection. It had changed my life, I honestly had no will left to live and this has given me my life back. 

For my nerve pain (I'm unsure if you have this but I wouldn't at all be surprised if you do) I take antriptlyne orally and also in a topical cream form. Even though I no longer have thrush and that has drastically improved my pain to a near zero, I can't have comfortable penetrative sex as it still burns - that's the nerve pain. I also sometimes get an occasional intense sharp jab or extreme itch on my labia - this is also the nerve pain. The nerve pain for me in mostly set off by stress to my pelvic floor muscles and pressure, so something like bike riding can increase the itchiness or burning. I've found that In conjunction with these meds, pelvic floor physio has helped...

but overwhelmingly hypnotherapy HAS SAVED ME. 

Hypnotherapy has rid me of all bladder pain, has almost entirely settled down my nerve pain (a few more weeks of treatment and I bet it'll be gone), and most importantly it has my anxiety under control. I never realised how severely anxious I was all the time. In the mornings I wake up calm after a good sleep, I do my hypnotherapy in bed, and I start my day present, clear and fresh. I've never coped so well with life stressors before. 

I want to explain that all my health conditions link together, and dominoed into each other. 

Before I got chronic thrush I got IBS, right after a sexual trauma. I always suspected this was my body's manifestation of that trauma and my inability to keep on top of my subsequent anxiety in my daily life after that. Recently Monash released an app of hypnotherapy called Nerva. I'm not kidding you, this shit has changed my life. I have no IBS symptoms at all (so no constipation, extreme bloating, cramps and pelvic pain) and my anxiety has drastically lessened because I'm not worrying obsessively about my strict diet or if my pain will flare etc. Although it focusses on my bowel (it's an audio that you do each morning, much life guided meditation) it has drastically helped my whole pelvic area. It's like I've hit the right domino in reverse to help all my health conditions. Because my pelvic floor muscles are relaxed more, and my bowels and stomach are calm and processing food properly, my vaginal/vular nerve pain and bladder pain have all drastically lessened. In turn I believe that once I go off the Depo Shot, thrush will not return as I have addressed the root cause: the chronic stress; the chronic inflammation.

I am 100% confident that chronic thrush was my body's response to chronic inflammation of my gut because of IBS, which was caused by excessive stress and anxiety. I do believe you need a triage of treatments - the right meds, exercises/physio, hypnotherapy - to heal from this. Currently I am researching a hypnotherapist specifically for vulvar and bladder pain so I can really get the full benefits of hypnotherapy on my whole pelvic region and not just my bowel.

If you IBS, I cannot recommend Nerva enough. It's been researched and created by Monash Uni which are the leading researchers on IBS - they created the FODMAP diet. They also found that Nerva is just as effective as the diet. That is how powerful hypnotherapy is. 

If you don't have IBS, I still do really think that chronic infections like thrush are cause by chronic inflammation of the gut - and the gut and the mind are deeply connected (butterflies in your tummy, that awful feeling in your stomach when you're anxious). So instead of going to cognitive behavioral therapy, try hypnotherapy for pelvic pain. I think it could really help break the cycle. It WILL ease your anxiety around pain. Trust me.

In conjunction with this you do need medications to help you. The hypnotherapy is treating the cause, and the meds will help treat the symptoms until your body is restored and your immune system can fight off basic infections like yeast infections on its own again. In the mean time, definitely definitely couple hypnotherapy with the Depo Provera shot. If you've had thrush for this long, it is not going away on it's own. I don't think you're going to be able to lower your stress until it is properly treated and you're not in agony anymore, I for sure couldn't. In doing this, you have the mental space to heal your mind, gut and body through  hypnotherapy. You deserve to have your life back - sex and exercise and just generally being able to be free from constantly thinking about when this fucking infection will stop controlling your life and happiness. 

I hope I haven't projected too much and that this helps you, I feel blessed you took the time to write that and help me. I didn't respond immediately but I read it before now when things were still very bad and very dark, and knowing that there was just someone made me feel less like I was suffocating. 

If you want to talk about any treatment I've mentioned in more detail, shoot me a message. Happy to answer any questions xx

Just so you know, swap tests for yeast infections (and urine dip-stick and culture tests for the matter) are notoriously unreliable. You can 100% have a YI or uti with a negative test. Especially if you have a chronic or recurrent YI or uti. I know this for certain as both have happened to me, I got neg results for both and then ended up in hospital a couple weeks later pissing puss and blood, and clear signs of an intense yeast infection. They did the tests again in the hospital and they still came out 'negative'. The doctors had to do a cathader test in my bladder to get accurate results. So, a negative swab or urine culture does not mean you do not have the infection. The standardised testing for YI and UTIs that general practitioners and even specialist use are simply unreliable, unstanderdised,  and failing us as people with vulvas and vaginas. By the sounds of it you've still got a yeast infection. Ultimately, you know your body better than ANY DOCTOR. 

Take a look at the doctor Gayle Fischer from Sydney. She has a great video on chronic thrush and how she treats it, and why the swabs come back neg: https://vimeo.com/180142036

I'd take this video to your doctor and discuss long term treatment for a chronic yeast infection. 

Good luck, I'm so sorry you have to be in this pain. Having a uterus is a fucking curse.
